project.name: Keystore Validator
project.summary: A privacy-first browser application for inspecting Android signing certificates and comparing an APK signer with a keystore certificate.
project.problem_statement: Android developers need to inspect the fingerprints in a JKS keystore and confirm whether a signed APK was signed by the same certificate without exposing private signing material.
goals: Read and display signing certificate fingerprints from a supplied JKS keystore.
Inspect an APK signature and compare its verified signing certificate with a selected keystore certificate.
Keep APKs, keystores, private keys, and passwords in the browser while hosting the application on a Vercel Hobby account.

included: Browser-local JKS inspection and alias selection
Browser-local APK signing certificate inspection and signature verification
SHA-256 certificate comparison with clear match, mismatch and unverifiable outcomes
Hobby-compatible static deployment and privacy-focused user experience
excluded: Uploading files, passwords, or private keys
Account creation, database, server-side file handling, or long-term storage
AAB inspection and Play Console integration for the initial release
Claiming APK install/update compatibility merely from matching a certificate

observations: Workspace was empty, with no existing Git repository or application files when discovery began.

notes: Standard mode selected for a security-sensitive browser application with signing and deployment constraints.
The user confirmed both APKs and keystores should be processed in the browser and APKs of at least 100 MB should be supported.
The user prefers Python but explicitly permits alternatives; TypeScript is recommended for the privacy-preserving browser runtime.
A generated JKS was read with keystore-go v4.5.0 via Go/WASM in Node; the resulting SHA-256 matched keytool and a wrong store password failed. Not tested in a browser.
Official apksigner is available locally in Android SDK build-tools 36.1.0; it has not yet been used to verify an APK fixture in this project.

APK experiment: apksig-go v1.1.0 disagreed with apksigner on an AOSP v2-only fixture for API 24-35; both rejected one tampered v1/v2/v3 fixture, while the candidate exposed verified signer flags despite an overall failure. Do not use candidate flags without overall verification and independent coverage.

facts.value: Extract JKS and APK signing certificate fingerprints and compare them.
Process JKS and APK files in the browser. Do not transmit private keys, files or passwords.
Support APKs of at least 100 MB.
Deploy to a Hobby Vercel account.
Python preferred; other languages may be proposed.
The workspace was initially empty and not a Git repository.
Vercel Functions impose a 4.5 MB request or response body limit.
Serve static assets from Vercel and process all selected files locally; comparison needs no server.

preferences: Python for development where appropriate; user explicitly permits an alternative.
selected: Web Workers and browser File/Blob APIs (design recommendation)
WebAssembly verifier only if the feasibility and security gates pass
alternatives: Python server: rejected for file handling because it would violate browser-local processing and server request size limits.
Python local scripts: optional for fixture generation or cross-checks; not a production file-processing backend.
Investigate Go/WASM plus TypeScript: a JKS alias/certificate experiment succeeded under Node, but browser and APK-verification gates remain open.

compatibility_evidence.statement: The Vercel function body limit makes typical large APK uploads unsuitable; static browser processing avoids the function upload path.
apksig-go advertises v1/v2/v3/v3.1 support and a browser WASM API; its browser integration copies the complete APK into Go memory and its correctness and size limits have not been verified here.
A browser JKS library that verifies store integrity and lists certificate aliases without decrypting private keys has not yet been validated.

A generated JKS was inspected with keystore-go v4.5.0 compiled to Go/WASM and executed under Node. The alias and certificate SHA-256 matched keytool; a wrong store password failed. This is a narrow proof, not a browser, malformed-input or APK verifier test.
compatibility_evidence.source: Local generated fixture: Go 1.27.4, Node 26.13.1, keytool; keystore-go https://github.com/pavlo-v-chernykh/keystore-go

compatibility_evidence.statement: A narrow Node/WASM differential experiment with apksig-go v1.1.0 and AOSP golden APKs found a disagreement on a valid v2-only APK: apksigner verifies it for API 24-35, while the candidate rejects it based on manifest minSdk 23. A tampered v1/v2/v3 APK was rejected overall by both, but individual signer verified flags remained true in the candidate. This is not a browser or security audit.
compatibility_evidence.source: AOSP golden fixtures https://android.googlesource.com/platform/tools/apksig/+/refs/heads/main/src/test/resources/com/android/apksig/ and local Android SDK build-tools 37.0.0 apksigner

features.name: Inspect a keystore
features.description: Read the selected JKS in a worker; request only the store password and expose aliases with public certificates.
acceptance_criteria: Detect and report unsupported or corrupt files without exposing secrets; validate JKS integrity when a password is provided and distinguish an incorrect password or integrity failure.
List certificate-bearing aliases; allow selection and display subject, issuer, validity dates, certificate SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints.
Do not request a separate private-key password or decrypt or export private keys just to display certificates.
Compare generated fixture results against keytool -list -v, including multiple aliases, trusted-certificate entries and wrong passwords.

features.name: Inspect and verify an APK
features.description: Read the APK locally, verify supported Android signing schemes and show verified signer certificate details.
acceptance_criteria: Show SHA-256 and SHA-1 certificate fingerprints and scheme verification results for each active signer if available; label certificate extraction and signature validity separately.

Verify applicable v1/v2/v3/v3.1 signatures and APK contents within the explicitly stated Android API range; unsupported schemes, rotation, malformed, tampered, unsigned and ambiguous cases must be identified and never reported as verified.
Cross-check verification results and signer fingerprints against official apksigner fixtures for supported API ranges, including valid, tampered, unsigned, multi-signer and rotated-key inputs.
Handle APK files of at least 100 MB on tested target browsers; report progress, allow cancellation and return a clear resource-limit error when needed.
Consider the verifier overall result and content integrity; individual signer verified flags alone cannot establish that an APK verifies.

features.name: Compare certificates
features.description: Compare the selected keystore certificate to the verified APK signer certificate locally.
acceptance_criteria: Use SHA-256 of the DER-encoded signing certificate for canonical identity; SHA-1 is display-only.
Show matched, mismatched, and unverifiable states; never assert signature validity or a successful verified match solely because an extracted certificate fingerprint matches.
For multiple signers or rotation show each signer and whether the selected certificate is active or historical; do not imply Android update compatibility from a single matching signer.
Explain Google Play app-signing keys versus upload keys when relevant.

features.name: Browser-local handling
features.description: Keep file contents and secrets on the user device.
acceptance_criteria: No request contains the APK, keystore bytes, private keys, password, alias or fingerprint; verify using browser network instrumentation.
Do not store sensitive input in browser storage or logs; keep temporary state in memory and drop references and terminate workers on reset.
Avoid third-party runtime scripts or telemetry; serve bundled assets from the same origin and use restrictive security headers compatible with the chosen WASM build.

features.name: Accessible and clear interaction
features.description: Provide an accessible, responsive interface for selecting files, entering the store password, and understanding results.
acceptance_criteria: Use labeled controls, keyboard navigation, visible focus and text alternatives; report loading, progress, success and failure accessibly.
Explain that files stay on the device and that password integrity validation is distinct from checking certificate expiry or APK signature validity.

features.name: PKCS#12 keystores
features.description: Detect PKCS#12 by contents even if a filename uses .jks, when a reviewed browser library supports it.
acceptance_criteria: Do not misidentify a PKCS#12 store as a JKS file; if unsupported, clearly report the format.
If enabled, verify behavior with keytool-generated fixtures and document alias and password limitations.

architecture.summary: Vercel serves a static TypeScript web UI and same-origin worker/WASM assets. User-selected APK and keystore bytes are read locally, with no file-processing backend. A verified browser-capable signing engine remains a required feasibility gate.

components.name: Vercel static hosting
components.description: Deliver first-party HTML, CSS, JavaScript and reviewed local WASM assets over HTTPS.

components.name: Browser UI
components.description: Collect files and store password locally, render progress and alias choices, and display signer and matching outcomes.

components.name: Browser worker
components.description: Own ephemeral local parsing, fingerprint calculation, cancellation and controlled error handling.

components.name: Signing inspection engine
components.description: Candidate JKS and APK verifier implementations; must pass feasibility, security, memory and differential tests before selection.

flows.label: Local File objects and store password only
Local certificate extraction and signature verification

datastores: None for user files, passwords or results.
authentication: No account or authentication required for the initial release.

security_privacy: Private keys and passwords must never leave the browser. APKs and keystores are processed locally.
Avoid private-key decryption for certificate inspection; no secrets in telemetry, logs, URLs or persistent storage.
Treat the delivered site and its dependencies as part of the trust boundary; restrict scripts and network connections, review updates, and avoid claims of absolute security.
constraints.offline: Processing should continue without network after all app assets are loaded; installable/offline-first service worker is not required initially.
constraints.monetization: No monetization requested; Hobby suitability for personal, non-commercial use must be checked before release.
performance: Support at least 100 MB APKs on measured desktop browsers, with worker responsiveness and bounded or clearly documented memory use.
Benchmark peak memory and time; browser memory constraints mean no universal size guarantee.
accessibility: Keyboard access, semantic labels, visible focus and readable error/progress messages; verify in target browsers.
localization: English initially as an assumption; use text resources that can later be localized.
deployment: Deploy a static build to Vercel Hobby; do not rely on server functions to receive files.
Keep a preview release and verify assets and security headers before promotion.
constraints.budget: Hobby account requested; usage-dependent bandwidth and build costs or limits must be checked against current Vercel terms.

workstream_independence.basis: 1 minus overlapping role pairs divided by all possible specialist pairs; a one-role team scores 1.0.

coordination_overhead.basis: Team-size, handoff, and project-complexity planning heuristic; lower is simpler.

context_requirements.basis: Planning estimate uses 2,500 supervisor input tokens, 1,500 per specialist, and 120 per feature or architecture component.

research_complexity.basis: Average number of catalogue research methods per selected role, multiplied by 1.5 and capped at 10.

integration_complexity.basis: Heuristic: 1 + 0.75 per specialist + 0.8 per overlap pair + 0.6 per manifest dependency + 0.25 per architecture component, capped at 10.

metrics.review_effort_basis: Uncalibrated points: 2 supervisor points, 1 per specialist, 0.5 per catalogue deliverable, and 0.25 per acceptance criterion.

risks.description: Extracted certificates can match even when an APK is tampered or signed under unsupported schemes.
risks.mitigation: Require cryptographic signature verification for a verified match; cross-test tampered and unsupported inputs against apksigner.

risks.description: Existing browser engines may not support required JKS integrity, all APK schemes, rotation or certificate extraction reliably.
risks.mitigation: Complete a separately reviewed proof of concept and differential tests; keep unsupported cases unverifiable and do not promise support without evidence.

risks.description: A 100 MB APK may trigger much larger memory use if JavaScript and WASM each retain copies.
risks.mitigation: Measure peak memory, explore chunked/random-access APIs, and publish tested browser limits; provide clear failures and cancellation.

risks.description: Compromised hosted JavaScript, dependencies, or browser extensions could expose secrets despite browser-local processing.
risks.mitigation: Review and pin dependencies; use same-origin assets and CSP; validate no sensitive traffic and document hosting trust.

risks.description: Google Play may sign distributed APKs with a different key from the developer upload key or a rotated key.
risks.mitigation: Identify active versus historical signers and explain upload versus app signing keys.

risks.description: Hobby terms, usage ceilings or browser limitations may not fit eventual usage.
risks.mitigation: Confirm personal non-commercial use, deployment limits, tested browsers and bandwidth before release.

risks.description: A candidate browser verifier rejects an apksigner-accepted v2 APK for the same API range; individual signer flags may remain true even when a tampered APK fails.
risks.mitigation: Investigate and correct or replace the engine, compare overall validity and signer identities against apksigner, and gate positive matches on the overall verified outcome.

assumptions.statement: Recent desktop Chromium, Firefox and Safari can be considered target browsers, subject to browser-engine tests.
assumptions.validation_action: Run the proof of concept and browser matrix before declaring support.

assumptions.statement: Users do not need accounts, shared history or server persistence.
assumptions.validation_action: Reconfirm before adding any persistent feature.

assumptions.statement: TypeScript is a suitable browser runtime, with Python optional only for local development and testing.
assumptions.validation_action: Verify worker/WASM integration, available tooling and reviewed library licenses during the feasibility spike.

decisions.question: Where will APK and keystore processing take place?
decisions.selected: Locally in the browser, with no private keys, passwords or files sent to the server.
decisions.rationale: User explicitly confirmed both file types must be handled in the browser.

decisions.question: Which application implementation language should be used?
decisions.selected: TypeScript for browser code; optional Python for offline fixture tooling.
decisions.rationale: The user permits an alternative to Python; browser execution avoids file uploads.

decisions.question: Which browser-compatible JKS and APK verification engines are suitable?
options: Independently evaluate and adapt a JKS parser and APK verifier
Select an alternative reviewed engine after prototyping
decisions.rationale: Candidates have not demonstrated integrity checks, safe alias access, complete signature/rotation semantics and memory behavior. No engine should be called verified before independent tests.

decisions.question: Which Android API range and signing schemes will the first release verify?
options: Set a tested API interval and explicitly list scheme coverage
decisions.rationale: Android scheme and key-rotation behavior varies by platform; an explicit tested interval is required for a valid verification claim.

decisions.question: Which browsers and device classes will be officially supported?
options: Recent desktop Chromium, Firefox, Safari after tests
decisions.rationale: Performance and WASM compatibility have not been measured.
